findings.fix_hint: make save_settings use the same relaxed validator (or the same loopback policy) as config load, or surface the rejection to the user
findings.problem: The new validator calls validate_arr_url_config, which deliberately accepts loopback literals (127.0.0.1, ::1) and localhost, so a TOML with url="http://127.0.0.1:7878" now loads cleanly. The settings POST handler (triggarr/web/routes.py:560-564) still runs every submitted instance URL through the strict validate_arr_url, and that function rejects is_loopback addresses (triggarr/web/validation.py:88). The form re-submits every instance's URL, so once any instance has the loopback URL that this layer now permits, every settings save fails: the handler logs a warning and sends a 303 back to the settings page without telling the user. The mismatch existed before, because the old load path did no validation at all. This diff turns the loopback allowance into the stated, documented contract while leaving the UI save path out of step with it.
findings.title: Loopback URL now allowed at config load, but the settings form still rejects it, so no settings can be saved
findings.why_it_matters: Same-host homelab users, the case this change sets out to support, cannot change any setting through the UI and get no feedback.

findings.fix_hint: catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config and log a friendly error naming the offending instance/url field before sys.exit(1)
findings.problem: load_settings (triggarr/config.py:227) builds Settings(**data). ensure_config (triggarr/config.py:370-373) only catches TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError, and its docstring says ValidationError propagates uncaught as a 'schema bug'. Before this diff, an existing triggarr.toml with a hand-edited or legacy URL loaded fine, even when the instance was disabled. Examples: a scheme-less 'radarr:7878', where urlparse reads 'radarr' as the scheme; 'http://0.0.0.0:7878'; any link-local literal. Now the validator raises ValueError for these, startup dies with a raw pydantic traceback from asyncio.run, and in Docker the container goes into a restart loop. The v2.2 migration path (detect_and_migrate_v22) also writes the migrated URL to disk before this validation runs. Unlike TOML corruption, this failure gets no friendly loguru message naming the config path and the instance. The rejection itself is described as intended hardening, so the finding is about how the failure is handled. pending: confirm whether rejected values such as scheme-less host:port or 0.0.0.0 appear in configs the project supports.
findings.title: A config URL the new validator rejects crashes startup with an uncaught ValidationError traceback
findings.why_it_matters: An upgrade turns a config that used to work, possibly with only a disabled instance at fault, into a crash loop with no clear message for the operator.

findings.fix_hint: handle ValidationError at the startup boundary and log a redacted message instead of letting the traceback print
findings.problem: A pydantic ValidationError's string form includes input_value. When this new validator rejects a URL at startup, the uncaught exception (ensure_config does not handle it) is printed by the default traceback handler to stderr, not through the loguru redacting sink. A URL carrying basic-auth userinfo, e.g. 'http://user:secret@169.254.1.5', would end up in container logs. reject_apikey_in_url already has the same exposure, so this is pre-existing in kind. pending: confirm the startup traceback is not routed through the redacting sink somewhere upstream (main/_run).
findings.title: The raw ValidationError at startup prints the full URL, including any user:pass@ credentials, outside the redacting log sink
findings.why_it_matters: Credentials embedded in a URL could leak into logs.

findings.fix_hint: In triggarr/config.py's ensure_config/load_settings, catch pydantic.ValidationError the same way TOMLDecodeError is handled (log a friendly, field-scoped error without echoing the raw URL, then sys.exit(1)) instead of letting it propagate uncaught.
findings.problem: The new `validate_url_ssrf` field_validator runs on every InstanceConfig.url unconditionally, including disabled instances (confirmed by the docstring and by `tests/test_config.py::test_instance_config_disabled_instance_metadata_url_still_raises`, which already asserts a disabled metadata URL raises ValidationError). Before this diff, InstanceConfig had no SSRF check at all, so any pre-existing triggarr.toml with a disabled instance whose url is a placeholder ("http://"), non-http scheme, or link-local/multicast/unspecified literal loaded successfully. I read `triggarr/config.py` (unchanged by this diff): `ensure_config`'s own comment at the time of this diff states 'OSError ... and pydantic.ValidationError (schema bug) continue to propagate uncaught', and `load_settings`/`ensure_config` only catch `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError`/`UnicodeDecodeError` -- not `pydantic.ValidationError`. `triggarr/__main__.py main()` only catches `KeyboardInterrupt` around `asyncio.run(_run())`. So a ValidationError raised by this new validator at config-load time propagates all the way out as an uncaught traceback, crashing the whole process before it ever binds the HTTP port -- the operator can't even reach the settings UI to fix it.
findings.title: New unconditional SSRF validator can crash the app at startup on pre-existing configs
findings.why_it_matters: On upgrade, any existing self-hosted deployment with a disabled *arr instance that happens to have a placeholder, malformed, non-http, or link-local/multicast URL in triggarr.toml will fail to start at all, with no recovery path short of manually editing the TOML file on disk -- a self-inflicted denial of service introduced purely by adding this validator without updating the startup error path.

agent_notes: Layering direction: triggarr/models/config.py (the config/domain model, imported by about 9 core modules) now depends on triggarr/web/validation.py through the function-local import at line 106. Normally that would be flagged as a separation-of-concerns inversion: web/routes.py already imports models.config, so this makes the models and web packages aware of each other. I did not flag it because the intent doc explicitly authorizes this exact import. .planning/phases/71-presentation-rewrite/71-02-PLAN.md, Task action, says: "Inside it, do a LOCAL import `from triggarr.web.validation import validate_arr_url_config` (module-level import would risk a circular import; web.validation imports nothing from models)." 71-PATTERNS.md line 149 repeats it. Intent confidence is about 0.95.

No import cycle exists, at module level or package level. triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty, and triggarr/web/validation.py imports only stdlib (ipaddress, re, urllib.parse). The plan's reason for the local import ('module-level import would risk a circular import') is therefore not true today: a top-level `from triggarr.web.validation import validate_arr_url_config` would be safe. The local import is harmless, but it hides the models-to-web dependency from static import scanners and from readers of the module header. Optional cleanup: hoist it to module level, or move the stdlib-only URL/SSRF helpers into a layer-neutral module (e.g. triggarr/validation.py or triggarr/models/) that both web/routes.py and models/config.py import. That would remove the inversion entirely. This is not a finding because the plan authorizes the current shape.

Precedent check: the only other function-local import from triggarr.web outside the web package is in triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532 and :538, which import web.routes. Those lazy imports really do avoid a cycle (routes imports scheduler at line 50). The new import in models/config.py is not following that pattern by necessity; there is no cycle to avoid.

Duplication (rule of three not met): validate_arr_url_config (web/validation.py:111) repeats validate_arr_url (web/validation.py:56) almost line for line. The only difference is that the is_loopback checks are dropped. That makes 2 copies, below the threshold, and the duplicate came from the prior commit 14eecb5, not this diff. If a third variant ever appears, refactor to one function with an allow_loopback flag. That would also stop the two blocklists drifting apart, which matters for security.

Two-tier validation is consistent with intent D-02. The web-form path (web/routes.py:561) stays strict with validate_arr_url, which rejects loopback. It then builds InstanceConfig, which runs the relaxed check, so the strict check always runs first on that path and the two never conflict there. Product note, not an architecture finding: if a user has a loopback URL (127.0.0.1) in triggarr.toml and then saves Settings through the UI, the strict check will reject the save with only a warning log and a redirect. That is the intended asymmetry per the plan, but the user may experience it as the save silently doing nothing.

Pattern consistency: the new validator follows the shape of the existing reject_apikey_in_url validator (@field_validator('url') + @classmethod + raise ValueError). It is defined after reject_apikey_in_url, so under Pydantic v2's definition-order rule the apikey rejection runs first, as the plan requires. It handles empty URLs consistently, since validate_arr_url_config returns (True, '') for '', which matches the default `url: str = ''`.

Blast radius (for the impact agent, not a design finding): because the validator is field-scoped and ignores `enabled`, any existing triggarr.toml containing a link-local, unspecified, multicast, or metadata URL, a non-http scheme, or a URL with no hostname will now fail at startup in every code path that builds Settings or InstanceConfig (startup.py, config.py, routes.py, tests/conftest.py fixtures). The intent doc authorizes this as hardening.

agent_notes: Safe-change classification: this diff routes InstanceConfig.url through an existing validator (validate_arr_url_config, validation.py:111) at model construction. It adds a control and removes nothing. reject_apikey_in_url still runs first, and the stricter validate_arr_url at routes.py:561 still guards the settings form.

Public API: there are no signature changes. InstanceConfig fields and defaults are unchanged, and the default url='' passes through the empty short-circuit at validation.py:138-139. So InstanceConfig() at routes.py:790 (add-instance) and every test that builds an empty instance are unaffected.

Import cycle: the function-local import of triggarr.web.validation is safe. validation.py imports only ipaddress, re and urllib.parse. After the first call the import is just a sys.modules lookup on every validation, which costs nothing at this scale (a handful of instances).

Blast radius by path: (1) Startup via ensure_config -> load_settings: any TOML URL that is now rejected aborts the process with an uncaught ValidationError (config.py:345 says this propagates). (2) Settings POST (routes.py:598): already-loaded instances passed load-time validation, and submitted URLs pass the stricter validate_arr_url first, so in practice the new validator never fires there. (3) Other SettingsModel/InstanceConfig rebuilds (add/delete/rename-instance routes) re-validate existing URLs that already passed at load. No new failure.

What changes for users: loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) is still accepted at load, which matches D-02. Cloud metadata hosts, link-local, unspecified (0.0.0.0) and multicast literals, non-http schemes and scheme-less 'host:port' strings are now rejected at load, even on disabled instances. Plain IPv4 100.64/10 (Tailscale CGNAT) is still accepted, except the exact 100.100.100.200 metadata IP. Homelab users on Tailscale are not affected.
Schema/migration: no DB or TOML schema change. There is no automatic migration for configs that now fail. The operator has to edit the TOML by hand, and the traceback does not explain how.
Performance: negligible. It is one urlparse and one ipaddress parse per instance at load or settings save.

Tests: I found no test fixtures using now-rejected URLs (0.0.0.0, ftp:// and scheme-less only appear in direct validate_arr_url tests in tests/test_validation.py). The existing suite should not break.
Verdict: shippable. The only follow-up is to wrap pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config so a rejected URL gives a friendly exit instead of a traceback or crash loop.

findings.fix_hint: Catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config() and log a friendly message naming the instance/field (without the URL value) before sys.exit(1), as _log_corrupt_config_and_exit already does for TOML errors; add a release note that invalid URLs now block startup.
findings.problem: The new field validator runs on every InstanceConfig.url, including on disabled instances. ensure_config() (triggarr/config.py:370-373) only catches TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError, and its docstring says pydantic.ValidationError 'continue[s] to propagate uncaught'. So if an existing triggarr.toml holds a URL the new check rejects, startup aborts with a raw traceback, and under a Docker restart policy the container restart-loops. One traced value: `http://0.0.0.0:7878`, put in by hand in the TOML. On Linux/macOS, connecting to the unspecified address reaches the local host, so it worked before. Now it hits validation.py:155 (`addr.is_unspecified`), which raises in config.py:110 and aborts. Other hand-edited values that now abort startup but were harmless before: a scheme-less `radarr:7878` (urlparse sees the scheme as 'radarr' and rejects it at validation.py:143) or any junk left on a disabled instance. Before this change, these failed per cycle (httpx.HTTPError caught in engine.py) or did nothing at all when the instance was disabled. The UI form path already rejected all of these through validate_arr_url (routes.py:561), so only TOML edited by hand is exposed. The docstring says this is intended hardening, which is why this stays capped. pending: confirm whether 0.0.0.0, scheme-less or disabled-with-junk URLs are inside the supported config contract (README/default template). If they are, this becomes a real upgrade regression at medium severity.
findings.title: Hand-edited TOML URLs that the new check rejects (including on disabled instances) now stop the daemon at startup with an uncaught traceback
findings.why_it_matters: When upgrading, a config that worked silently is now refused with no clear guidance. In a Docker deployment this looks like a crash loop rather than a config error.

findings.fix_hint: If a friendly startup handler is added, log `exc.errors(include_input=False)` rather than str(exc).
findings.problem: Pydantic ValidationError messages include `input_value=<url>`. If a hand-edited TOML URL such as `ftp://user:pass@host` or `http://user:pass@0.0.0.0` fails the new check, the full value, credentials included, lands in the uncaught startup traceback. On the settings POST path, routes.py:600 logs `Invalid settings rejected: {exc}`, but the stricter validate_arr_url at routes.py:561 normally rejects such URLs first, so that path is mostly shielded. reject_apikey_in_url already has the same behaviour, so this is a pre-existing pattern that the diff extends to one more class of rejected input. pending: show a URL with userinfo that passes routes.py:561 but fails validate_arr_url_config. That cannot happen, because the config variant is strictly looser. So the only real exposure is the startup traceback for hand-edited TOML.
findings.title: Rejected URL value (possibly with embedded basic-auth credentials) appears in the ValidationError text that routes.py logs and the startup traceback prints
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md says to never log secrets. Basic-auth credentials in a reverse-proxy URL are secrets that the redacting sink does not know about.
